Self-evaluation (self-perspective)
“the degree to which people like or dislike themselves”
 People who have a positive core self-evaluation see 
themselves as effective, capable, and in control
 Believe in their inner worth and basic competence
 People who have a negative core self-evaluation tend to 
 dislike themselves 
 question their capability
 view themselves powerless
 No control on environment.

Locus of Control 
“refers to people’s beliefs about the amount of control they 
have over their lives”.
Internals
Individuals who believe that they can control what happens to 
them. 
Externals
Individuals who believe that what happens to them is controlled 
by outside forces such as luck or chance.

Machiavellianism (Mach)
“Degree to which an individual is pragmatic, maintains 
emotional distance, and believes that ends can justify 
means”.
•High Machs manipulate more, win more, are persuaded less, and
persuade others more than do low Machs (Christie & Geis, 1970).
•High Machs make good employees in jobs that require bargaining
skills (labor negotiation) or that offer substantial rewards for winning.

“A personality trait that measures an individuals ability to adjust his or her 
behavior to external, situational factors”.
❖High SM are capable of changing their behavior and expressions according to the situations. 
❖High HM progress faster in their career than low SM.
❖Highly sensitive to situational cues, and are able to behave differently in different situations.
❖High SM are sometimes called “Chameleon” (Kilduff & Day, 1994).
❖High SM are more likely to be promoted both within the organizations and external position 
(Kilduff & Day, 1994) and receive successful career monitoring
Self-Monitoring (SM)

Risk-Taking
 High Risk-taking Managers
◦ Make quicker decisions
◦ Use less information to make decisions
◦ Operate in smaller and more entrepreneurial organizations
 Low Risk-taking Managers
◦ Are slower to make decisions
◦ Require more information before making decisions
◦ Exist in larger organizations with stable environments
 Risk Propensity
◦ Aligning managers’ risk-taking propensity to job requirements should be 
beneficial to organizations.
